subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: Should generic LiteLLM Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT be treated as provider-owned recoverable session/request-shape failure, context overflow, or ordinary schema rejection?
rationale: The same HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT status can mean several incompatible provider failures, so automation should not choose broad recovery semantics without maintainer intent and live provider proof.

options.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery
options.body: Add LiteLLM/Vertex-specific classification for the proven raw shape and verify user copy plus lane cleanup in a live or high-fidelity provider path.

options.title: Wait for live reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open but require a real LiteLLM Vertex beta artifact before changing classification semantics.

options.title: Keep as schema rejection
options.body: Treat the generic INVALID_ARGUMENT as ordinary provider validation failure and document that users should start a fresh session or change model route.

recommendation.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery
recommendation.body: Add LiteLLM/Vertex-specific classification for the proven raw shape and verify user copy plus lane cleanup in a live or high-fidelity provider path.

likelyOwner.reason: He is connected to both the LiteLLM plugin surface and the merged provider-error normalization path.
